clue.text: Consecutive houses may be

definitions.meaning: one straight after another, with no gap between
terraced houses built sharing a rear wall, typical of old industrial towns

explanation.surface: An estate agent remarks on how adjoining houses can stand in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, back-to-back houses are rows of cheap terraces joined at the rear as well as the sides, built in industrial towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that follow one another without a break are said to come in an unbroken run, the idiom for successive.

clue.text: Polish aficionado

definitions.meaning: to shine up a surface by rubbing

explanation.surface: An enthusiast from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine metal is to rub it bright, and an enthusiast is a fan, e.g. a film fan.

clue.text: Drug I found among company staff

indicators.note: the letter is located inside the other word

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick, a staff

explanation.surface: A narcotic is discovered among a firm's employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' means employees in the surface, but here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stimulant narcotic, from the coca plant.

clue.text: Completely wreck it like a heretic — or a tyrant

parts.note: to total a car is to wreck it beyond repair
taken as written
Arian describes a follower of Arius, a famous heretic

explanation.surface: Someone smashes something up in the manner of a heretic or despot.
explanation.walkthrough: Arius was a 4th-century priest whose teaching was condemned as heresy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator ruling with absolute power is the archetypal despot, i.e. tyrant.

clue.text: French army split, with one in support

parts.note: the BEF, British Expeditionary Force, was the army sent to fight in France

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the word for split

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart, split
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An army in France divides, with one soldier staying loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French army' is loose: the BEF was the British army sent to France in both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to stand by and help them.

clue.text: Mark that distinguishes century — long time

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century (Latin centum, a hundred)
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A hallmark that sets apart a period of a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective with 'time', but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is prestige or a distinguishing seal, a stamp of distinction.

clue.text: Oddly unsteady, so treated

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters (first, third, fifth, seventh) of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Something wobbly has, curiously, been dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handled or employed has been put to use, a synonym for treated in the sense of dealt with.

clue.text: Slight injury's no handicap

definitions.meaning: a minor graze or nick on the skin
a golfer or runner starting with no advantage is said to play off this

explanation.surface: A minor wound is not a real disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a player who plays off this has a handicap of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a minor wound, and a player with zero handicap starts from the line.

clue.text: Small group of soldiers exhibiting indifference

definitions.meaning: a unit sent off for a special duty

explanation.surface: A squad of troops shows a lack of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached unit of troops, and also aloofness or emotional distance.

clue.text: Opposite view of expert

parts.note: a facet is one aspect or way of viewing a matter
taken as written
an ace is a top performer, an expert

explanation.surface: A contrary opinion from a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view of expert' looks like a single idea, a specialist's opinion; 'view' is in fact one aspect of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people meeting in person stand opposite each other, each looking at the other.

clue.text: COurage required to deal with icy roads

definitions.meaning: pluck or determination, as in showing true backbone

definitions.text: required to deal with icy roads
definitions.meaning: sand and small stones spread on frozen roads for traction

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed to drive on frozen roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is both resolve and nerve, and the coarse material spread by gritting lorries on winter roads.

clue.text: A despair, possibly, shown in this poem?

parts.note: these two words are what a word for heaven becomes when it is lost, that is, scrambled

explanation.surface: A gloomy feeling is perhaps expressed in this epic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the letters of A DESPAIR rearranged give the first word of the answer, and 'lost' is a common anagram signal; 'possibly' flags the trick. Milton's epic is also about despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's 17th-century epic about the Fall of Man is the best-known long poem in English.

clue.text: It was instrumental in eliminating half the force

indicators.note: removing half of a word means the last four of its eight letters are dropped

parts.note: violence is physical force

explanation.surface: Something played a key role in reducing a police force by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eliminating half' cuts ENCE from VIOLENCE. 'It was instrumental' is a playful definition: the viol is an old instrument, largely superseded.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol is an early bowed stringed instrument, now mostly historic, hence 'was'.

clue.text: Stiff line I cast out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: An angler finds the line they cast is rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LINE I CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that does not stretch or give is rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: Nice smelling stuff sweets possess

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the sweet course
to have is to own, possess

explanation.surface: Some confectionery has a pleasant scent.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is a British informal word for the pudding course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a scented lotion splashed on the face after a shave, a fragrance.

clue.text: Short shot, going round part of golf course backwards

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a fling is an attempt, a go or shot at something

indicators.note: the word for part of the golf course is read from end to start

parts.note: the tee is the area each hole is played from

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a weak stroke while playing a hole in reverse order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short shot' suggests a golf stroke that falls short, but 'Short' is the definition and 'shot' means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleeting moment is brief, lasting only a short time.

clue.text: Sound of at-home's kept within limits

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the phrase with its outer letters trimmed off

explanation.surface: A noise is heard at a social gathering held in moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept within limits' means drop the outer letters of OF AT-HOME, leaving FATHOM. An at-home is a party given in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound the sea is to measure its depth, the same verb as plumb.

clue.text: Crack spinner keeps score down

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits above the other, so the spinner word comes first

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
to score is to cut a notch or groove

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler holds down the run total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' means excellent, as in a crack shot. 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler, but it is a toy top.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack troops are first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: 20 policemen in Ireland

indicators.note: the police abbreviation goes inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP stands for military police

explanation.surface: A number of police officers are stationed in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to the answer at 20 across, a word for a realm, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a realm ruled by a single sovereign power.

clue.text: Bird is going up and over boarding house

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: on means on top of, over

explanation.surface: A bird is ascending and flying over a guest house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a continental guest house or small hotel offering board.

clue.text: Party — servant in control

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a minion is a lowly subordinate or servant

explanation.surface: A political party with a lackey in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is sovereign authority, rule over a territory or people.

clue.text: Rail against breaking into one nicker

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the short letter forces its way into the run of letters

parts.note: a nicker is a horse's soft whinny, a neigh
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a thief breaking into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail against' looks like the definition, but 'against' gives V; 'nicker' is not the thief (or the British slang for a pound) but a horse's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest angrily, to denounce bitterly.

clue.text: Verbally purchase paper boat

indicators.note: spoken out loud, signalling that the answer sounds like the words

parts.note: to buy a ream, a bundle of 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone orders writing paper by phone for the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbally' signals that 'buy ream' said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: Feeling one isn't as excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person is not as thrilled as others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges ONE ISN'T AS; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A physical perception, such as touch or warmth, is a sense impression or feeling.

clue.text: Begrudge representative giving nothing away

indicators.note: giving ... away together say a letter is given up from the word
with giving, signals that something is removed from the word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic representative
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A diplomat resents having to keep quiet about secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving nothing away' suggests a discreet envoy, but it means ENVOY loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: To grudge someone something is to resent their having it, i.e. to be jealous.

clue.text: Antique silver chap collected

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Ed, short for Edward, is any man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: An old silver piece a man has collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very old.

clue.text: Enthusiastic prima donna retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: An eager opera star has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DIVA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen and eager.

clue.text: Finishing off sentry-go, I'd fall out

indicators.note: the letters break ranks and form up in a new order, a military command apt for sentries

explanation.surface: A soldier announces that sentry duty is over and they will fall out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall out' rearranges SENTRYGO and ID. Sentry-go is old army slang for sentry duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to finish off, kill or end something completely.

clue.text: Nothing less than a fiver, say, toback this mount

indicators.note: to back means the pieces are read in reverse order, from end to start
less signals a letter is taken away from the following note

parts.note: a fiver, five pounds, is an example of a banknote
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gambler will stake at least five pounds on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less than' looks like 'at least'; it is O removed from NOTE, giving NTE. A + NTE is reversed by 'toback' (printed 'to back').
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, a mountain, and mount is the same thing.

clue.text: Tie the knot, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Tie the knot, in more ways than one

parts.words: Tie the knot, in more ways than one
parts.note: to marry is idiomatically to tie the knot, and a hitch is literally a kind of knot, so both readings fit

explanation.surface: Getting married, and literally tying a knot too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to marry, and a hitch is a sailor's knot, so it is a literal tying as well.
